endpoint_hypotheses.edges: A,B,C are positive integers with gcd(A,B,C)=1

individual_face_factorization.proof: For one face write A=g_AB*a, B=g_AB*b with gcd(a,b)=1. The face-square identity gives (D_AB/g_AB)^2=a^2+b^2 and D_AB/g_AB is integral. Coprime a,b have opposite parity, so a+ib and a-ib are coprime in Z[i]: any common odd Gaussian prime would force a common rational prime divisor of a,b, while 1+i would force equal parity. Their product is an integer square. Unique factorization in Z[i] therefore gives a+ib=epsilon_AB*Z_AB^2. The other two faces are identical cyclically.

two_adic_bookkeeping.exact_parity: exactly one of A,B,C is odd
two_adic_bookkeeping.proof: no face can have two odd legs because 1+1=2 mod 4 is not a square; primitivity excludes all three edges even
two_adic_bookkeeping.consequence: the Gaussian prime 1+i is supported in at most one rational edge-gcd factor g_AB,g_AC,g_BC and is absent from every gcd between two distinct face Gaussians or their conjugates

private_edge_gcd_support.statement: every Gaussian prime dividing g_AB is absent from F_AC,conj(F_AC),F_BC,conj(F_BC), and cyclically for g_AC and g_BC
private_edge_gcd_support.proof: For odd underlying p, p|g_AB gives p|A,B and primitivity gives p not dividing C, so the other two face Gaussians reduce to nonzero multiples of C modulo any Gaussian prime over p. For p=2, A,B even forces C odd, so A+/-iC and B+/-iC have opposite coordinate parity and are not divisible by 1+i.

locator_proof: Each ideal equality follows by adding/subtracting one generator after multiplication by the unit i where needed; e.g. F_AB-i*F_BC=A+C. Conjugating the six identities gives all remaining orientations.

cross_face_square_gcd_theorem.statement: for any two distinct literal face Gaussians, with either one independently conjugated, their gcd ideal in Z[i] is a square ideal; moreover 1+i does not divide that gcd
cross_face_square_gcd_theorem.proof: Use F_jk=epsilon_jk*g_jk*Z_jk^2. By private_edge_gcd_support no Gaussian prime from either rational g_jk can divide the other distinct face. Hence every common Gaussian prime occurs in both elements only through square factors, so the minimum valuation in the gcd is even. The 1+i case is excluded explicitly by the two-adic bookkeeping.
cross_face_square_gcd_theorem.generator_form: because Z[i] is a PID, every such gcd generator is a unit times H^2 for some H in Z[i]
cross_face_square_gcd_theorem.odd_shared_prime_locator: odd shared primes may lie only over rational primes dividing the corresponding A+/-B, A+/-C, or B+/-C locator, but every shared Gaussian-prime exponent in the gcd is even

squareclass_output.cross_face_shared_squareclass: trivial: every distinct-face gcd is square and contributes no shared prime squareclass
squareclass_output.remaining_support: the three rational edge-gcd squareclasses g_AB,g_AC,g_BC are pairwise coprime, private to their own faces, and remain moving symbolic endpoint quantities at this layer
